answer: A charcoal kiln fired from one timber stand buys a seat when its pulse of smoke rises on time: at dawn a newcomer seals one kiln at a named oasis grove, and two wardens weigh the charcoal against the stand's yield table the same week. A kiln that yields short by more than five pounds, or smoke that never rises, voids the claim and burns a 500 POA bond. Each firing costs a $170 kiln fee plus a $60 weighing fee, so 100 fakes need 100 kilns, $23,000 in fees and 50,000 POA in bonds.
